title: TalkVerse official README
claims: TalkVerse-5B is an audio-driven LoRA trained on the TalkVerse corpus and paired with the Wan2.2-TI2V-5B base plus Wav2Vec2-large-xlsr-53-english.
Single-video inference takes an image, audio file and prompt; offload_model=True and t5_cpu are documented as VRAM-saving flags for consumer GPUs such as RTX4090.
The batch script exposes INFER_FRAMES=120 and GUIDE_SCALE=6.5; the README describes the baseline as capable of minute-long generation.
The generate script saves video first and then merges the input audio, so the audio is an external track rather than a native generated soundtrack.

resources.gpu: Consumer GPU example is RTX4090; no measured card stated
resources.precision: Wan2.2-TI2V-5B plus TalkVerse-5B audio LoRA; Wav2Vec2 encoder

limitations: No L4/A100 wall time, peak VRAM, host RAM, seed or fixed-quality comparison; repository code/dataset/weights use Snap Inc. Non-Commercial License.

title: TalkVerse paper
claims: The paper describes a Wan2.2-5B audio-driven baseline using a (t,h,w)=(4,16,16) VAE, sliding-window generation, motion-frame context, FramePack, and reference-image positional embeddings for long-video continuity.
It evaluates 40-second long videos at 25fps, corresponding to 1000 frames, and reports an author claim of about 10x lower inference cost than Wan-S2V-14B.

The paper says the 5B model can underperform on complex/extreme hand articulation and full-body motion; it also reports that LoRA training preserved better visual quality than full DiT fine-tuning for articulated hands and objects.

resources.resolution: paper dataset includes 720p/1080p clips; evaluation resolution not specified in cited abstract lines
resources.precision: Wan2.2-5B DiT + audio cross-attention/LoRA; exact inference dtype not stated
resources.workflow: TalkVerse sliding-window S2V with FramePack/context history

limitations: The 10x cost statement is author-reported relative to Wan-S2V-14B and has no L4/A100 runtime row; quality claims are paper evaluation, not the requested hardware acceptance test.

title: VACE: All-in-One Video Creation and Editing
claims: The official repository describes VACE as an all-in-one model for reference-to-video, video-to-video, and masked video-to-video composition.
Wan2.1-VACE-1.3B is listed around 81x480x832 and Wan2.1-VACE-14B around 81x720x1280; the README says input resolution is flexible but optimal sizes are bounded.
The repository dates the full 1.3B and 14B model release to May 14, 2025 and provides preprocessing, inference, and benchmark assets.

resources.precision: Wan VACE checkpoint; repository does not give a low/mid hardware benchmark

limitations: Model size/resolution table is a task contract, not a VRAM or quality score; no L4 or single-A100 wall time is reported.

title: VACE UserGuide
claims: VACE-recognizable inputs are src_video, src_mask, src_ref_images, and prompt; src_video may be depth, pose, flow, gray, layout or in/outpainting content, while white mask areas are generated and black areas retained.

The preprocessing table names DepthVideoAnnotator, FlowVisAnnotator, PoseBodyFaceVideoAnnotator, ScribbleVideoAnnotator, LayoutBboxAnnotator, LayoutTrackAnnotator and FrameRefExpandAnnotator, including first/last frame and first/last clip extension modes.
The guide says super-long videos are trimmed or uniformly sampled to around 5 seconds and recommends generating 5-second clips one by one with firstclip extension for temporal consistency.
limitations: The guide defines input semantics and a long-video procedure but does not state preprocessing GPU/RAM cost or identity/action quality scores.

The CLI exposes offload_model, t5_cpu, dit_fsdp, src_video, src_mask, src_ref_images, sample_steps, sample_shift, and sample_guide_scale; single-GPU mode defaults offload_model to true when unspecified.
The default model path is Wan2.1-VACE-1.3B and default size is 480p.

resources.precision: config dtype / optional CPU offload

It says 1.3B can technically generate 720P but has limited high-resolution training and is generally less stable, recommending 480P for optimal performance.

title: VACE 1.3B killed on A10G 24GB with 16GB RAM
claims: The reporter used an AWS g5.xlarge with NVIDIA A10G 24GB VRAM and 16GB RAM; the VACE 1.3B 480p/81-frame pipeline was killed while creating the pipeline.
The reporter states that 1.3B at 480p required about 21GB RAM and worked after moving to a 32GB RAM instance.
The reporter then states a 5-second 480p generation took about 15 minutes and nvidia-smi showed about 19GB VRAM usage.

title: VACE 14B OOM and checkpoint pairing issue

The same user reports about 89% VRAM but green noise/pixelated output at 480p/81 frames after pairing VACE 14B module with a Wan2.1 I2V base; Kijai says VACE must be paired with the T2V model, not I2V.
The user later reports 350 frames taking 4.5 hours with 14B blockswap versus about 40 minutes with 1.3B.

title: Wan2.2 official README: Wan-Animate
claims: Wan-Animate takes a video and a character image and has animation mode (character image mimics motion) and replacement mode (character image replaces the input-video character).
Animation preprocessing uses pose retargeting and optional FLUX image editing; replacement preprocessing uses iterations, k, w_len, h_len and replace_flag for mask processing.

Single-GPU generation uses animate-14B with refert_num 1; replacement can use relighting LoRA. The README warns against Wan2.2 LoRA models on Wan-Animate because weight changes may cause unexpected behavior.

resources.gpu: single-GPU command; no model-author card specified
resources.precision: Wan2.2-Animate-14B; optional relighting LoRA in replacement

limitations: No L4/A100 timing or peak memory in the text-readable README; GPU efficiency table is an embedded image not used here.

title: Wan-Animate preprocessing UserGuider
claims: Preprocessing requires pose detection (YOLOv10m and ViTPose wholebody), with SAM2 for replacement mask extraction and FLUX.1-Kontext-dev for optional enhanced retargeting.
Animation mode can use no retargeting, basic retargeting or enhanced retargeting; the guide says retargeting is not guaranteed and intermediate pose outputs should be checked.
Replacement mode pose retargeting is disabled by default; body-proportion mismatch can produce artifacts/deformation, and the simplified mask extractor is for single-person videos only.
Lower fps may improve generation efficiency but can cause stuttering/choppiness; resolution_area applies to preprocessing and generation.
limitations: The guide names extra preprocessing models but gives no extra GPU/RAM measurements or preprocess wall time.

title: Wan-Animate preprocess_data.py
claims: The script resolves det/yolov10m.onnx and pose2d/vitpose_h_wholebody.onnx from ckpt_path; replacement additionally resolves sam2/sam2_hiera_large.pt and enhanced retargeting resolves FLUX.1-Kontext-dev.
The CLI exposes resolution_area, fps, replace_flag, retarget_flag, use_flux, iterations, k, w_len and h_len, and calls ProcessPipeline with these settings.
limitations: CLI source confirms dependency paths and parameters but does not measure preprocessing resources.

title: InfiniteTalk official README
claims: InfiniteTalk is described as audio-driven video-to-video and image-to-video with unlimited-length generation; it supports 480P and 720P, streaming/clip modes, TeaCache and APG.
The required stack is Wan2.1-I2V-14B-480P base, TencentGameMate Chinese Wav2Vec2 audio encoder, and MeiGen-InfiniteTalk single/multi audio-condition weights.
The README exposes num_persistent_param_in_dit=0 for very-low-VRAM, FP8 quantization for single GPU, FusionX 8-step and LightX2V 4-step options.

The README says V2V can be unlimited but camera movement is not identical; SDEdit improves camera accuracy but causes color shift; I2V from one image is good up to about one minute, with stronger color shift beyond one minute; FusionX can worsen color shift after one minute and reduce ID preservation.

title: MultiTalk official README
claims: MultiTalk takes a reference image, prompt and one or more audio streams, supports single/multi-person conversation, singing and cartoon, and lists 480p/720p output with up to 15 seconds.

The current code section says single-GPU inference supports 480p while 720p requires multiple GPUs; the model was trained on 81-frame videos at 25fps, with up to 201 frames possible but weaker prompt following at longer lengths.

The README announces low-VRAM 480p on one RTX4090, INT8 quantization, TeaCache, APG, and FusionX/LightX2V 4–8-step acceleration; its efficiency section says multi-person results were evaluated on A100 GPUs.
An A100 Google Colab example is linked, but the linked notebook is not text-readable without login.

title: ComfyUI Wan SVI 2 Pro FLF continuation node
claims: The node combines SVI 2 Pro motion continuity with Wan2.2 first/last-frame control, allowing continuation from an existing video with a next target frame, prompt, or both; included workflow groups can be duplicated beyond seven clips.
